settingDefinitions.comment: setting definition part only, does not restore anything

setting.name: Serial Port
setting.description: >Enable or Disable Serial Port (COM)

setting.name: LAN 1 Controller
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Onboard LAN1 Contoller.

setting.name: Onboard USB Controllers
setting.description: >[Enabled] Onboard USB controllers are enabled and work as configured. [Disabled] Onboard USB controllers are disabled. All connected USB devices are not available: - external keyboard and mouse - keyboard and mouse via IRMC - internally connected USB devices

setting.name: Legacy USB Support
setting.description: >Enables Legacy USB support. AUTO option disables legacy support if no USB devices are connected. DISABLE option will keep USB devices available only for EFI applications.

setting.name: Launch PXE OpROM Policy
setting.description: >Controls the execution of UEFI and Legacy PXE OpROM.

setting.name: FLASH Write
setting.description: >Enable or Disable FLASH write on Legacy boots.

setting.name: LAN
setting.description: >Allows the system to be switched on via a LAN wakeup.

setting.name: Skip Password on WOL
setting.description: >Password entry is not required on automatic Wakeup from LAN.

setting.name: Password on Boot
setting.description:
>On Every Boot - The password prompt appears on every boot.
On First Boot - The password prompt appears on cold boot only.
Disabled - The password is always taken from NV storage and there is no password prompt displayed.

setting.name: Wake On LAN boot
setting.description: >[Boot Sequence] Use Boot Sequence order after Wake On LAN. [Force LAN Boot] Force LAN boot after Wake On LAN (Option "Launch PXE OpROM" must be enabled to actually force a network boot).

setting.name: Bootup NumLock State
setting.description: >Select the keyboard NumLock state

setting.name: Active Processor Cores
setting.description: >Number of cores to enable in each processor package.

setting.name: Enhanced SpeedStep
setting.description: >When enabled, OS sets CPU frequency according load. When disabled, CPU frequency is set at max non-turbo.

setting.name: Execute Disable Bit
setting.description: >When disabled, forces the XD feature flag to always return 0.

setting.name: Intel Virtualization Technology
setting.description: >When enabled, a VMM can utilize the additional hardware capabilities provided by Vanderpool Technology.

setting.name: Boot Removable Media
setting.description: >This option enables/disables support for booting to removable devices, such as USB flash drives.

setting.name: Hyper-Threading
setting.description: >Enables Hyper-Threading (Software Method to Enable/Disable logical Processor threads).

setting.name: TPM Support
setting.description: >Enables or Disables TPM support. O.S. will not show TPM. Reset of platform is required.

setting.name: TPM State
setting.description: >Turn TPM Enable/Disable. NOTE: Your Computer will reboot during restart in order to change State of TPM.

setting.name: VT-d
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O (VT-d) by reporting the I/O device assignment to VMM through DMAR ACPI Tables.

setting.name: Intel TXT(LT) Support
setting.description: >Enables or Disables Intel(R) TXT(LT) support.

setting.name: Quiet Boot
setting.description: >Enables or disables Quiet Boot option

setting.name: Skip PPI during next Boot
setting.description: >Skip Physical Presence confirmation during the next Boot

setting.name: SATA Mode Selection
setting.description: >Determines how SATA controller(s) operate.

setting.name: Pending TPM operation
setting.description: >Schedule TPM operation. NOTE: Your Computer will reboot during restart in order to change State of TPM.

setting.name: ECC Memory Error Logging
setting.description: >Configure ECC Memory Error Logging Support.

setting.name: PCI Error Logging
setting.description: >Enable/Disable PCI Error Logging.

setting.name: Turbo Mode
setting.description: >Turbo mode allows a CPU logical processor to execute a higher frequency when enough power is available not exceed CPU defined limits.

setting.name: Boot error handling
setting.description: >Determines what to do on boot errors: Pause and wait for key OR continue.

setting.name: PERR# Generation
setting.description: >Enables or Disables PCI Device to Generate PERR#.

setting.name: SERR# Generation
setting.description: >Enables or Disables PCI Device to Generate SERR#.

setting.name: LAN 2 Controller
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Onboard LAN2 Contoller.

setting.name: USB Port Control
setting.description: >Configures how USB ports are enabled. [Enable all ports] All USB ports are enabled. [Disable all ports] All USB ports are disabled. [Enable front and internal ports] All rear USB ports are disabled. [Enable rear and internal ports] All front USB ports are disabled. [Enable internal ports only] All external USB ports are disabled. [Enable used ports] All unused USB ports are disabled.

setting.name: USB transfer time-out
setting.description: >The time-out value for Control, Bulk, and Interrupt transfers.

setting.name: Primary Display
setting.description: >Selects which graphics controller has connected the primary display.

setting.name: Internal Graphics
setting.description: >The BIOS detects automatically if the internal graphics controller can be disabled, but it can manually be forced to enabled or disabled.

setting.name: LAN 1 Oprom
setting.description: >Controls which OptionROM will be loaded for the respective onboard LAN port. [Disabled] No OptionROM is loaded. [PXE] Load the PXE OptionROM. [iSCSI] Load the iSCSI OptionROM.

setting.name: LAN 2 Oprom
setting.description: >Controls which OptionROM will be loaded for the respective onboard LAN port. [Disabled] No OptionROM is loaded. [PXE] Load the PXE OptionROM. [iSCSI] Load the iSCSI OptionROM.

setting.name: ASPM Support
setting.description: >Configures Active State Power Management (ASPM) energy saving. [Disabled] No energy saving. Best stability. [L1 Only] Tradeoff between stability and energy saving.

setting.name: Network Stack
setting.description: >Enable/Disable UEFI Network Stack

setting.name: Ipv4 PXE Support
setting.description: >Enable Ipv4 PXE Boot Support. If disabled IPV4 PXE boot option will not be created

setting.name: Ipv6 PXE Support
setting.description: >Enable Ipv6 PXE Boot Support. If disabled IPV6 PXE boot option will not be created

setting.name: Secure Boot Control
setting.description: >Secure Boot can be enabled if 1.System running in User mode with enrolled Platform Key(PK) 2.CSM function is disabled

setting.name: Factory Default Key Provision
setting.description: >Provision factory default keys on next system re-boot while platform is in Setup Mode

setting.name: Launch CSM
setting.description: >This option controls if CSM will be launched.

setting.name: Launch Slot 1 OpROM
setting.description: >Enable or disable option ROM execution for device in slot 1.

setting.name: Launch Slot 2 OpROM
setting.description: >Enable or disable option ROM execution for device in slot 2.

setting.name: Launch Slot 3 OpROM
setting.description: >Enable or disable option ROM execution for device in slot 3.

setting.name: Launch Slot 4 OpROM
setting.description: >Enable or disable option ROM execution for device in slot 4.

setting.name: Power-on Source
setting.description: >[BIOS Controlled] Power-on sources are controlled by BIOS. Also valid for ACPI operating systems. [ACPI Controlled] Power-on sources are controlled by an ACPI operating system.

setting.name: Above 4G Decoding
setting.description: >Enables or Disables 64bit capable Devices to be Decoded in Above 4G Address Space (Only if System Supports 64 bit PCI Decoding).

setting.name: Keep Void Boot Options
setting.description:
>[Enabled] Keeps the FW boot options for devices no longer connected to the system. Useful to keep the position of the void boot options in the boot order list until next re-connection to a device.
[Disabled] Remove the FW boot options for devices no longer connected to the system.

setting.name: Boot option filter
setting.description: >This option controls what devices system can boot to.

setting.name: Launch PXE OpROM Policy
setting.description: >Controls the execution of UEFI and Legacy PXE OpROM.

setting.name: Launch Storage OpROM policy
setting.description: >Controls the execution of UEFI and Legacy Storage OpROM

setting.name: Launch Video OpROM policy
setting.description: >Controls the execution of UEFI and Legacy Video OpROM.

setting.name: Other PCI device ROM priority
setting.description: >For PCI devices other than Network, Mass storage or Video defines which OpROM to launch.

setting.name: PXE Boot Option Retry
setting.description: >This will continually retry NON-EFI based PXE boot options without waiting for user input.

setting.name: Hardware Prefetcher
setting.description: >To turn on/off the MLC streamer prefetcher.

setting.name: Adjacent Cache Line Prefetch
setting.description: >To turn on/off prefetching of adjacent cache lines.

setting.name: DCU Streamer Prefetcher
setting.description: >Enable/Disable DCU Streamer Prefetcher.

setting.name: Package C State limit
setting.description: >Package C State limit

setting.name: Limit CPUID Maximum
setting.description: >This should be enabled in order to boot legacy OSes that cannot support CPUs with extended CPUID functions.

setting.name: PXE boot wait time
setting.description: >Wait time to press ESC key to abort the PXE boot

setting.name: Check controllers health status
setting.description: >Enables or disables checking of health status of hardware components

setting.name: Password Severity
setting.description:
>Standard - Password skip jumper can be used to clear a lost password.
Strong - Password skip jumper inoperable. In case of a lost password, unlocking only possible via service.

setting.name: PCI Slot 1
setting.description: >PCI Slot Control

setting.name: PCI Slot 2
setting.description: >PCI Slot Control

setting.name: PCI Slot 3
setting.description: >PCI Slot Control

setting.name: PCI Slot 4
setting.description: >PCI Slot Control

setting.name: Change Settings
setting.description: >Select an optimal settings for Super IO Device

setting.name: Secure Boot Mode
setting.description: >Secure Boot mode selector. 'Custom' Mode allows for more flexibility changing Image Execution policy and Secure Boot Key management.

setting.name: New Boot Option Policy
setting.description: >Controls the placement of newly detected UEFI boot options, for non removable media

setting.name: SW Guard Extensions (SGX)
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Software Guard Extensions (SGX)

setting.name: X2APIC Opt Out
setting.description: >Enable/Disable X2APIC_OPT_OUT bit

setting.name: Power Limit 1 Override
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Power Limit 1 Override. If this option is disabled, BIOS will program the default values for Power Limit 1 and Power Limit 1 Time Window.

setting.name: Power Limit 1 Window
setting.description: >Power Limit 1 Time Window value in seconds. The value may vary from 0 to 128. If the value is 0, default values will be programmed (28 sec for Mobile and 1 sec for Desktop). Indicates the time window over which TDP value should be maintained.

setting.name: Power Limit 2 Override
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Power Limit 2 Override. If this option is disabled, BIOS will program the default values for Power Limit 2.

setting.name: Platform PL1 Enable
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Platform Power Limit 1 programming. If this option is enabled, it activates the PL1 value to be used by the processor to limit the average power of given time window.

setting.name: Platform PL1 Time Window
setting.description: >Platform Power Limit 1 Time Window value in seconds. The value may vary from 0 to 128. If the value is 0,g default values will be programmed Indicates the time window over which Platform TDP value should be maintained.

setting.name: Platform PL2 Enable
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Platform Power Limit 2 programming. If this option is disabled, BIOS will program the default values for Platform Power Limit 2.

setting.name: Power Limit 3 Override
setting.description: >Enable/DisablePower Limit 3 override. If this option is disabled, BIOS will leave the default values for Power Limit 3 and Power Limit 3 Time Window.

setting.name: Power Limit 3 Time Window
setting.description: >Power Limit 3 Time Window value in Milli seconds. The value may vary from 3 to 64(max).Indicates the time window over which Power Limit 3 value should be maintained. If the value is 0, BIOS leaves default value

setting.name: Powet Limit 3 Duty Cycle
setting.description: >Specify the duty cycle in percentage that the CPU is required to maintain over the configured Power Limit3 time windows.

setting.name: Power Limit 4 Override
setting.description: >Enable/Disable Power Limit 4 override. If this option is disabled, BIOS will leave the default values for Power Limit 4.

setting.name: DVMT Shared Memory Size
setting.description: >Select DVMT 5.0 pre-allocated (fixed) memory size used by the internal graphics controller.

setting.name: DVMT Total Graphics Memory Size
setting.description: >Select DVMT 5.0 total memory size used by the internal graphics controller.

setting.name: CPU C states
setting.description: >Enable or disable CPU C states

setting.name: Port 61h Bit-4 Emulation
setting.description: >Emulation of Port 61h bit-4 toggling in SMM

setting.name: Port 60/64 Emulation
setting.description: >Enables I/O port 60h/64h emulation support. This should be enabled for the complete USB keyboard legacy support for non-USB aware OSes.

setting.name: PM Support
setting.description: >Enable/Disable PM Support
